* "The American Soldier" is named as ''[[TIME]]'' magazine's "[[Time Person of the Year|Person of the Year]]". The periodical's editors chose the anonymous soldier to represent the 1.4 million men and women serving in the [[United States Armed Forces]]. [http://www.time.com/time/personoftheyear/2003/] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060213194152/http://www.time.com/time/personoftheyear/2003/ |date=2006-02-13 }} [http://story.news.yahoo.com/news?tmpl=story&cid=514&e=3&u=/ap/20031221/ap_on_re_us/time_person_of_the_year] [https://www.usatoday.com/news/nation/2003-12-21-time-person_x.html] [http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,106330,00.html] [http://www.guardian.co.uk/uslatest/story/0,1282,-3533323,00.html] [https://web.archive.org/web/20050903175926/http://www.iol.co.za/index.php?click_id=22&art_id=qw1072012685498B211&set_id=1] [http://www.hindustantimes.com/news/181_503640,00050001.htm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930055532/http://www.hindustantimes.com/news/181_503640,00050001.htm |date=2007-09-30 }}
* Citing increased "chatter" regarding potential terrorist attacks over the holiday period, the [[U.S. Department of Homeland Security]] raises its [[terrorism]] alert level from "elevated" (yellow) to "high" (orange). [https://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=domesticNews&storyID=4028248] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050408033547/http://www.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=domesticNews&storyID=4028248 |date=2005-04-08 }}
* A senior French police source claims [[Diana, Princess of Wales]] was pregnant when she was killed in a car crash in Paris in [[1997]]. A [[Clarence House]] spokesperson for [[Charles, Prince of Wales|The Prince of Wales]] refuses to comment on the issue. [[Mohamed Al-Fayed]], the father of Diana's partner [[Dodi Al-Fayed]] had long insisted that Diana was pregnant with Dodi's baby and that she was murdered to stop her from giving birth. [https://web.archive.org/web/20041209001924/http://news.independent.co.uk/uk/this_britain/story.jsp?story=475166] [https://web.archive.org/web/20070825170430/http://www.itv.com/news/1839342.html]
* Quoting an unnamed senior British military intelligence officer, a report in the Sunday Express (Britain) claims that before [[Saddam Hussein]] was captured by US troops, he had already been discovered by the [[Patriotic Union of Kurdistan]] (PUK). Kurdish forces had been alerted to his location by a member of the al-Jabour tribe whose daughter had been raped by Saddam's son [[Uday Hussein]]. [http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2003/12/21/1071941609659.html]
* Retired Gen. [[Wesley Clark]] presented 4,000 petition signatures to qualify for [[South Carolina]]'s Democratic presidential primary ballot today. He's the second of the nine candidates for the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nomination to file for the [[February 3]] ballot. Campaign workers for Sen. [[John Kerry]] of [[Massachusetts]] gave the state Democratic Party a check for $2,500 last week to qualify.
